checks.finding: T-012 (new this round) is classified Risk: medium, but its Scope/Planned Files/Done When make it the sole implementer of the write-side of Security Boundary B5: it is the only task that mutates `tests/fixtures/structural-fixture-corpus/` (Planned Files: 'this task's own live-model refresh writes/updates recorded-response entries via the corpus's own refresh_procedure field ... never mutated by the gating suite itself'), the exact artifact security-spec.md's Trust Boundaries table names as B5's asset ('a malformed recorded artifact must never be silently treated as passing') and whose STRIDE row names the precise threat T-012 sits on: 'A malformed or subtly-altered recorded-response fixture in the structural-fixture-corpus is silently treated as a passing structural-compatibility comparison' (security-spec.md STRIDE Analysis, B5). Unlike its closest sibling, T-002 (rated high specifically because 'a silent defect here ... lets an unreviewed, possibly-regressed legacy-behavior snapshot get silently canonized as the new compatibility oracle every other suite in this feature trusts', with a structural CI-env-var/--approved-by fail-closed guard verified by AC-040/AC-041), T-012's Done When has no equivalent structural gate on the corpus content it writes -- only a schema-shape check ('Any corpus entry the refresh path writes follows structural-fixture-corpus/v1's own documented schema ... never mutating a gating-suite-consumed entry outside this sanctioned path'). A schema-valid but semantically wrong corpus entry from a defective T-012 refresh would not be caught by the canonicalizer's 'parse failure = hard suite failure' mitigation (design.md Design Decisions, 'Structural-comparison seam') and would silently become T-004's new comparison baseline for its gating suite -- a 'silent defect causes material harm' surface per risk-classification-policy.md's own high-tier definition, and the identical oracle-corruption pattern that earns T-002 its high tier. This risk boundary was not independently scrutinized before this round: in the prior tasks.md the AC-031 refresh logic was still folded into T-004 (Risk: high) itself; the round-2 split into a standalone T-012 is the first point at which this functionality's own risk tier was set independently, and it was set to medium without addressing the B1/B5 asymmetry above.

findings.finding: T-012 is classified Risk: medium while being the sole implementer of Security Boundary B5's write path (the only sanctioned mutator of `tests/fixtures/structural-fixture-corpus/`, T-004's gating-suite comparison oracle), with no structural fail-closed human-approval guard on that write analogous to sibling task T-002 (Risk: high for the token-for-token analogous 'silently canonized as the new compatibility oracle' pattern under Boundary B1, guarded by promote-golden-baseline.sh's CI-env-var/--approved-by refusal and verified by AC-040/AC-041). A schema-valid-but-wrong corpus entry from a defective T-012 refresh would not be caught by the canonicalizer's parse-failure-is-a-hard-fail mitigation and would silently become T-004's new expected baseline -- exactly security-spec.md's own named STRIDE threat for Boundary B5 ('A malformed or subtly-altered recorded-response fixture in the structural-fixture-corpus is silently treated as a passing structural-compatibility comparison') and risk-classification-policy.md's own 'silent defect causes material harm' high-tier trigger. Recommend re-evaluating T-012 for Risk: high (Required Workflow: tdd) or adding an explicit, structurally-enforced review/approval gate on corpus writes comparable to T-002's promote-golden-baseline.sh guard before confirming Risk: medium.
